title: unique_id: SystemTime::now() unwrap_or_default seeds all IDs to epoch on clock failure
description: SEQ is initialized with SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default().as_nanos() as u64 (line 17). If duration_since() fails (clock before epoch, which cannot happen on sane hardware), unwrap_or_default() silently seeds all IDs at nanosecond 0. Two processes seeded at 0 with the same counter state would generate colliding file names in a shared queue directory. Should be: if clock is before epoch, use a compile-time fallback (e.g. 0 + a process-unique salt), or panic during initialization with a clear error. The current silent fallback is the worst option: it generates wrong behavior silently.
